sourceAnchors.sourceLine: Before application runtime, the development pipeline must pass a real Chromium isolation canary using synthetic loopback servers. It checks redirects, custom routes, independent browser/API contexts and rejected proxy overrides; denied targets must receive zero requests and zero TCP connections. A worker-owned loopback proxy on an ephemeral port permits only the fixed `127.0.0.1:8080` upstream. Playwright's HTTP fetch transport requires CONNECT; only the exact `127.0.0.1:8080` authority is accepted, with a literal fixed upstream connection and bounded connection/cleanup. The canary requires positive approved CONNECT evidence from guarded page and API requests. All other CONNECT authorities are rejected. Temporary canary and proxy ports are recorded in retained run receipts and closed by their harness owner; they are not persistent application routes. Service workers, WebSockets and caller overrides of browser networking are rejected.
